definition: Slow to act or speak because of doubt, worry, or uncertainty.
example: On her first day at the new school, Priya was hesitant to raise her hand in class.
nuance: Hesitant suggests pausing out of doubt or nerves, while reluctant stresses not wanting to do something at all.
prompt: A swimmer stands at the edge of a high diving board for the first time.
options: The hesitant swimmer peered down at the water and stepped back twice before jumping.
The hesitant swimmer raced to the end of the board and dove off without a moment's pause.
Completely sure of herself, the hesitant swimmer never thought twice about the drop.
The hesitant diving board creaked and bent under the swimmer's weight.
reasons: Stepping back and delaying the jump shows doubt holding her back.
Diving off instantly shows no delay or doubt, which is the reverse of the word.
Total confidence and no second thoughts contradict the uncertainty the word implies.
A board cannot feel doubt; the word describes people or their actions, not objects.

practice.prompt: A boy is offered a dish he has never eaten before at a family dinner.
options: His grandmother called Marco hesitant because he asked for a third helping right away.
Marco gave the unfamiliar stew a hesitant sniff before taking a tiny taste.
Marco took a hesitant gulp and emptied the whole bowl in seconds.
Marco was hesitant about the stew because he had been craving it all week.
reasons: Asking for more at once shows enthusiasm, so the label fits the opposite behavior.
A cautious sniff followed by a small taste shows uncertainty slowing him down.
Gulping down a full bowl quickly shows eagerness, not caution.
Craving something makes a person eager, so there is no doubt to cause a delay.
